first.notice: Accepted. The review marker now points at 76126979. A draft decision card exists for the maintainer; nothing was posted.

findings.rationale: In Node.js, console.assert only writes a message to stderr when the condition is falsy; it never throws. So this file always exits successfully even if sumTo(0) returned a wrong value, meaning the PR's only test provides no regression protection and CI could not detect a breakage of sumTo.
findings.correction: Replace console.assert with an assertion that actually fails the test, e.g. import assert from 'node:assert'; assert.strictEqual(sumTo(0), 0); or use the project's test framework.

findings.rationale: The parameter is typed number with no validation. sumTo(Infinity) loops forever because i <= Infinity is always true, hanging the process; fractional inputs are silently truncated (sumTo(2.5) returns 3, i.e. it sums to floor(n)). The intended contract is undocumented.
findings.correction: Guard the input, e.g. if (!Number.isFinite(n)) throw new RangeError('n must be finite'); and either reject fractional values or document that non-integers are floored.
